**Measured effect (paired "both" runs vs original, identical seeds):** select-half (128 problems) 5.47% → 32.81% (+27.3 pp, SE 4.1); on the untouched confirmation sets: confirm_1 7.81% → 28.91% (+21.1 pp, 27 wrong→right, 0 right→wrong) and confirm_2 6.25% → 27.34% (+21.1 pp, 27 wrong→right, 0 right→wrong). The same edit preserved full (unconstrained-length) thinking — unlike a stronger "amplify </think>" variant that scored 46.9% but made 94/128 answers open with an immediate `</think>`, i.e. it skipped thinking, which the task forbids; that variant (and a late-layer-only version, and a single-example rank-one "ready-to-close" edit, which produced garbage) was explicitly rejected in favour of the confirmed direction-removal edit.

**Why it should generalise:** the failing circuit (the Wait-direction attractor) is input-independent in direction; the edit removes a spurious token-writing pathway rather than memorising answers. Both held-out practice confirmation sets improved by the same +21 pp with zero correct→wrong flips, and the model's remaining behaviour (long thinking that still truncates ~65–72% of the time, now using other connective words) degrades gracefully.

**Caveats:** the gain comes purely from escape from the loop; it does not fix arithmetic/reasoning slips. A further termination gain exists (amplifying the </think> direction on late down_projs reaches ~45%) but it was measured to skip thinking wholesale and was not submitted. Residual loops with ordinary words ("So", "If", "Let's") remain the dominant remaining failure mode.
